summary: Tier 1 challenge-enabling hygiene shipped: Corrections Policy, Right of Reply, and Cite As section all live and linked from About.

items.headline: Corrections Policy published
items.body: docs/Corrections-Policy.md documents what gets corrected vs re-graded, how to report a correction, the changelog 'type: correction' schema, the response timeline, and what corrections do not do. Linked from About. Closes the Tier 1 corrections-policy item per the bias-resistance plan.

items.headline: Right of Reply channel published
items.body: docs/Right-Of-Reply.md provides a documented channel for federal ministries, agencies, watchdogs, and named third-party analysts cited in any dimension's evidence chain to submit critiques. Documents who it's for, what it is not, the review process, what gets reflected, and the limits and scope. Linked from About. Closes the Tier 1 right-of-reply item.

items.headline: Cite As section added to About
items.body: About now includes a Cite As section providing a citation format for journalists, researchers, and other dashboards. Includes the dashboard URL, rubric version, and pointer to the open-source dimensions.json for per-dimension citations. Closes the Tier 1 citation-format item.

summary: Bias-Resistance-Protocol drafted: codifies eleven principles, three emergent disciplines, and pre/post-cycle review templates into a recurring methodology gate.

items.headline: Bias-Resistance Protocol v1.0 drafted
items.body: docs/Bias-Resistance-Protocol.md codifies what the May 2026 audit cycle learned. Eleven principles with built/partial/new status. Three new disciplines that emerged from this cycle's fixes: must-have-prior-substantive-view before adding a source, thread-existing-challenge-before-adding-new, and modifiers-explain-what-does-not-COUNT-not-what-should-not-HURT. Pre-cycle checklist, post-cycle review template, per-grade-move party-symmetry line, public-surface backlog, and audit re-run cadence. Reflects actual findings rather than preempted speculation per the planning doc's sequencing rule.

summary: Bias-resistance audit doc closed out as a true closure memo; raw audit output untracked to match its gitignore status.

items.headline: Bias-resistance audit doc now reads as closure memo
items.body: docs/Bias-Resistance-Audit-2026-05.md was written before the Phase 1 fixes shipped, so it read as forward-looking. The doc now opens with a Closure summary mapping all four shipped fixes to their version + commit references (v5.28 7b4136a, v5.29 b746abb, v5.30 b06e9de), each Fix section header carries a Shipped status, and Next steps now lists the actual follow-on work (Bias-Resistance-Protocol, Methodology FAQ, Tier 1 hygiene, full language audit, Skeptic Path UI, perceived-bias survey, Phase 2 foundational audit). No findings changed.

items.headline: Raw audit output untracked from git
items.body: scripts/output/ is gitignored by design. The raw audit output (scripts/output/bias-audit-raw-2026-05.txt) was tracked before the gitignore entry took effect; this commit untracks it to match the policy. The output remains regenerable via node scripts/audit-bias-resistance.mjs.

summary: Bias-resistance audit Fix 4 + Fix 5: event-driven trigger convention surfaced in methodology doc; Immigration modifier-absence documented as intentional.

items.headline: Trigger sourcing conventions documented in the scoring rubric
items.body: The methodology doc now explains the three trigger sourcing patterns (sourceUrl, internalRef, event-driven) so readers can interpret trigger panels correctly. Event-driven triggers are deliberate placeholders for source-families whose specific URLs become knowable only when the event occurs. Closes audit Fix 4: surface the convention rather than hide it.

items.headline: Immigration modifier absence documented as intentional
items.body: The Immigration dimension's judgmentDetail now explicitly states why no External Constraint modifier is applied: the absorption strain that prompted the correction was inherited from prior policy decisions, but the current government's response to those conditions is what this dimension grades. Prior conditions do not soften the assessment of current action. Closes audit Fix 5 in the conservative direction (document intent) rather than expansive direction (add a softening modifier).

summary: Bias-resistance audit Fix 3: defenders perspectives now cite named institutional sources, closing the critics-attributed / defenders-anonymous asymmetry on five dimensions.

items.headline: Defenders perspectives now name their authoritative sources
items.body: The audit found that five dimension defenders blocks cited zero or few named sources while critics blocks cited 2-6. Affordability Response, Carbon Pricing Policy, Climate & Environment, Housing Supply, and Economic Policy Response now bring named institutional sources into their defenders prose (PBO, OECD, CCI, CER, Department of Finance, Treasury Board Secretariat, CMHC, Smart Prosperity Institute) where authoritative defensive reasoning already supported the position. No grades, thresholds, or substantive claims changed; attribution surfaced.

summary: Bias-resistance audit Fix 1b + 1c: PBO independent challenge sources added to Immigration and Defence & Trade grade-moving chains.

items.headline: Immigration cites PBO Demographic Implications report
items.body: Added the PBO 'Demographic Implications of the 2026-2028 Immigration Levels Plan' (RP-2526-025-S) to the Immigration dimension's sources list and attached it as a sourceRef on the PR target (2026-2028) metric. Closes the audit finding that Immigration's grade-moving chain lacked an independent challenge source. No grade, threshold, formula, or modifier rule changed.

items.headline: Defence & Trade cites PBO Major Capital Priorities assessment
items.body: Added the PBO Spring Economic Update Major Capital Priorities assessment (NT-2627-003-S) to the Defence & Trade dimension's sources list and attached it as a sourceRef on the NATO spending (2025e) metric. PBO directly assesses Canadian defence funding adequacy including the NATO commitment. Closes the audit finding that Defence & Trade's grade-moving chain lacked an independent challenge source. No grade, threshold, formula, or modifier rule changed.

summary: Independent challenge sources now sit directly under key Major Projects and Climate metrics.

items.headline: Major Projects and Climate evidence chain tightened
items.body: Already-cited independent sources now appear under the specific Key Metrics they qualify. Major Projects threads Fraser Institute and Angus Reid into the headline-investment / credit-claiming metric; Climate & Environment threads CCI, IISD, CBC, and The Conversation into the emissions-pathway and ECCC-capacity metrics. No grades, thresholds, formulas, or source pool changed.

items.headline: Bias-resistance audit updated after Fix 1a
items.body: The audit raw output and findings doc now treat visible metric source links as grade-moving evidence. Major Projects and Climate & Environment no longer carry the no-independent-challenge flag; Defence & Trade and Immigration remain open for separate review.

summary: Ethics trigger traceability repaired and the first bias-resistance audit artifacts drafted.

items.headline: Ethics Annex A trigger now points to the working filing
items.body: The Ethics & Transparency up-trigger for the PM's Brookfield accounting now links to the Ethics Commissioner Annex A PDF already used in the dimension's source list, replacing the dead PMO backgrounder link.

items.headline: Bias-resistance audit artifacts drafted
items.body: A planning doc, reusable audit script, raw audit output, and first May bias-resistance audit now separate real methodology risks from script artifacts. The audit frames future fixes around threading existing challenge sources into grade-moving claims before adding new sources.

summary: May source-link sweep: nine broken citation URLs replaced with current canonical pages.

items.headline: Broken source links repaired across nine citations
items.body: The May link-rot scan flagged nine cited URLs returning 404. Replacements pulled from canonical equivalents on pm.gc.ca, canada.ca, climateinstitute.ca, fraserinstitute.org, and angusreid.org. Affected dimensions: Carbon Pricing Policy (consumer carbon price, industrial pricing), Fiscal Health (capital gains cancellation), Housing Supply (Canada-Ontario Partnership, apprenticeship), Immigration (2026-2028 levels plan), Major Projects (Fraser MPO commentary), and Promise Delivery (Angus Reid one-year review). The remaining PM Annex A trigger link was handled in the follow-up traceability repair.

summary: Recurring source checks now name event-driven watches, climate scans, promise spot-checks, and source-role review.

items.headline: Event-driven source watch list added
items.body: The recurring source checklist now calls out rating agencies, climate and carbon policy events, defence and NATO releases, major federal announcements, and bill-status movement as checks that should run when events appear instead of waiting for a fixed quarterly cadence.

items.headline: Long-tail source coverage made explicit
items.body: Climate and carbon sources, policy institutes, academic sources, journalism sources, stalled and abandoned promise links, source-role consistency, and archive fallback checks now have named rows in the recurring checklist rather than being hidden inside broad deep-search language.

items.headline: Public location wording removed
items.body: The About page now describes the project as independent without listing a project location.

summary: Source-coverage hygiene: the May refresh is now documented as a targeted refresh, not a full recertification.

items.headline: May source coverage ledger added
items.body: A new May source-coverage ledger records which source families were checked, which dimensions were refreshed, which pilot-packet links were spot-checked, and which gaps remain open. The May notes were also renamed from source-pull notes to source-refresh notes so the title matches the actual scope.

items.headline: Recurring source checklist created
items.body: A new recurring-source checklist defines the monthly, quarterly, and twice-yearly source checks for future cycles, plus the automation backlog for PBO RSS, StatCan value diffs, LEGISinfo, MPO diffs, polling pages, and Ethics Commissioner report changes.

items.headline: Inter-rater packet snapshot clarified
items.body: The pilot packet and reviewer invite now state that the rater is grading a frozen 2026-04-30 snapshot, not the current live dashboard. The results template now pre-fills the published snapshot grades to avoid comparing a rater against newer live data.

items.headline: Pilot source link spot-check completed
items.body: The 18 inter-rater packet source links were checked before recruitment. One broken House ETHI PDF link was replaced with the working House DocumentViewer report page in both the pilot packet and the live Ethics source list.

summary: May grade review: Fiscal Health moved up to C, Major Projects denominator was reconciled to the official MPO list, and Housing Supply kept D after the March starts check.

items.headline: Fiscal Health moved D → C
items.body: The Spring Economic Update lowered the projected FY 2025-26 deficit to $66.9B, and PBO now says both fiscal anchors are on track. The file stops at C because the deficit remains above the B threshold and PBO still flags capital-budgeting, interest-burden, and defence-cost caveats.
drivers: PBO says the deficit-to-GDP anchor is on track, declining from 2.1% in 2025-26 to 1.4% by 2030-31
PBO says the operating-balance anchor is projected to be met by 2028-29
Caveats remain on capital-budgeting definitions, rising interest burden, and omitted anticipated defence spending

items.headline: Fiscal-anchor promise moved back into progress
items.body: The operational-budget-balance promise now reads In Progress rather than Stalled. The evidence is still caveated: PBO says the anchors are on track, but also says the capital/operating classification needs more detail.

items.headline: Major Projects cohort denominator corrected to 15 projects
items.body: The official MPO page lists 15 referred projects and separates out transformative strategies. The dashboard now counts only the 15 projects in the cohort denominator; documented post-designation advancement remains 2 of 15, so the grade holds at C.

items.headline: Housing starts trigger reviewed and held
items.body: CMHC March 2026 starts showed a 235,852 monthly SAAR but a 248,378 six-month trend. Because CMHC says the trend measure smooths volatile monthly readings, the dashboard does not treat the one-month dip as firing the <240K down trigger while the trend remains above 240K.

summary: May source refresh: approval polling and several source metrics updated without changing grades.

items.headline: Approval Signal refreshed
items.body: Four recent approval polls from Abacus Data, Leger, and Angus Reid Institute were added. The 60-day sample-size-weighted display still rounds to 57% approve and 31% disapprove, net +26.

items.headline: Fiscal and labour metrics refreshed
items.body: Fiscal Health now uses the Spring Economic Update's $66.9B FY 2025-26 deficit projection and PBO's assessment that new measures offset most later fiscal room. Economic Policy now references the April Labour Force Survey.

items.headline: Affordability CPI refreshed
items.body: Affordability Response now uses March 2026 food-store CPI at 4.4% year over year. April CPI is scheduled for release on May 19.

items.headline: Manual review queue logged
items.body: The targeted source refresh flagged two calls for the grade-review phase: reconciling the Major Projects public project list with the live cohort, and deciding how the Housing Supply starts trigger should treat March CMHC starts data.

summary: Mobile evidence polish: the Major Projects full project list now uses readable project cards on phones.

items.headline: Major Projects list no longer needs sideways scrolling on mobile
items.body: The full project pipeline still uses the compact table on desktop, but phone-width screens now show stacked project cards with tranche, stage date, and source link visible in each card. No grades, scores, thresholds, source data, or methodology changed. The cohort denominator was later reconciled to 15 on 2026-05-13.

summary: Mobile card-spacing polish: dimension cards now have a little more breathing room while scrolling on phones.

items.headline: Scorecard cards breathe more on mobile
items.body: The mobile scorecard and tracker grids now use a wider gap between cards, responding to Reddit feedback that the grade cards felt cramped while scrolling. No grades, scores, sources, promise statuses, or methodology changed.

summary: Traceability polish: event-driven trigger sources now say so directly in the scoring drawer.

items.headline: Non-clickable trigger sources now identify event-driven evidence
items.body: Six grade-move triggers that depend on future events now label their source line as event-driven, so readers can distinguish evidence that already has a one-click source from evidence that would only exist if the trigger fires. No grades, scores, thresholds, source lists, or promise statuses changed.

summary: Scoring-boundary disclosure: the About and Methodology pages now state what the dashboard can and cannot score.

items.headline: About page now names the dashboard's scoring boundary
items.body: A new section explains that the dashboard scores sourceable federal action, documented commitments, published thresholds, and observable outcomes, not leadership style, symbolic politics, popularity, forecasts, or valuable outcomes that lack enough public evidence to grade.

items.headline: Methodology limits now address measurable-vs-valuable risk
items.body: The rubric limits now say plainly that the model can only score what can be inspected through public evidence, rather than estimating weakly evidenced qualities by proxy.

items.headline: README feature list reconciled with the live app
items.body: The removed Print / Export PDF feature is no longer advertised, and the About feature now mentions the new scoring-boundary disclosure.

summary: Mobile UX bug-fix bundle: trust frame is now global, evidence chips no longer clip on phones, drill-downs return readers to the scoreboard on close, and the project pipeline gives a clear scroll cue.

items.headline: What this is / what this isn't moved into the global header
items.body: The scope frame previously lived inside the Scorecard tab only. It now sits between the dashboard title and the scoreboard, so a reader who lands on Promises, Change Log, or Rubric still sees what the dashboard is and is not for.

items.headline: Print / Export PDF button removed
items.body: The button printed a screen-style page that was not optimized for paper. Removed alongside its print stylesheet rather than left as an unfulfilled promise.

items.headline: Promise tab evidence links no longer clip on mobile
items.body: Source and Status evidence chips on expanded promise rows now wrap their text instead of forcing a single line, so long source labels stay fully visible on narrow screens.

items.headline: Promise rows show a stronger details affordance
items.body: The previous pale chevron next to each promise now reads as a darker '▸ Details' / '▾ Hide' label so it is obvious that rows expand for evidence.

items.headline: Project pipeline now signals horizontal scroll
items.body: The Major Projects pipeline table now carries a 'Scroll right for stage date and source links →' caption and a right-edge fade gradient on narrow screens, so readers do not miss the source column.

items.headline: Tab rail signals overflow on narrow phones
items.body: On phones where 'Scorecard / Promises / Change Log / Rubric / About' overflows the rail, a small fade gradient on the right edge cues that more tabs sit off-screen.

items.headline: Closing a drill-down scrolls back to the scoreboard
items.body: On phones, hiding the score-derivation panel or the approval-signal drill-down now scrolls the page back to the scoreboard so readers do not have to manually backtrack.

items.headline: Evidence-link styling unified
items.body: Trigger-level evidence links and the project pipeline source column are now consistently rendered as 12px bold blue links, while file-level source chips remain the larger filled-chip treatment. Two visual treatments instead of five.

items.headline: Approval Signal card shares the same footer slot as the grade cards
items.body: 'See polls & sources' moved from the body of the Approval card into the footer slot, so all four scoreboard cards land their action affordance at the same vertical position.

items.headline: Trend arrows are now accessible
items.body: The improving / stable / declining arrows next to each dimension name now carry aria-labels and tooltips so the trend is announced to screen readers and visible on hover, not only via the legend.

items.headline: Duplicate freshness marker removed
items.body: Each dimension card showed both a 'Last reviewed' pill on the card face and an 'Updated YYYY-MM-DD' line above Key Metrics. The pill is now the single canonical freshness marker.

items.headline: Grade-change marker is now within the readable font floor
items.body: The '(was X)' previous-grade marker bumped from 11px to 12px so the mobile font-size floor catches it; the design tokens disallow body text below 12px.

summary: Mobile disclosure placement fix: headline-score and approval drill-downs now open directly under the tapped card on phones.

items.headline: Score math opens where mobile readers expect it
items.body: On narrow screens, the Household Impact and Full Policy Audit derivation panels now render immediately below the card that opened them instead of after all four headline boxes.

items.headline: Approval details follow the same mobile pattern
items.body: The Approval Signal drill-down now uses the same responsive ordering, so tapping the card scrolls to the poll details directly under that card on phones.

summary: Internal traceability pass: triggers whose evidence lives inside the dashboard now jump to their evidence home instead of remaining grey labels.

items.headline: Internal evidence homes are now clickable
items.body: Major Projects triggers can jump to the project pipeline, Flagship Delivery triggers can jump back to the home-dimension grid, and Promise Delivery triggers can open the Promises tab.

items.headline: Defence & Trade split tripwire tightened
items.body: The split rule now covers both opposite movement and widening sub-score gaps, and it explicitly uses two consecutive monthly review cycles as the promotion test.

items.headline: Ethics trigger language made more concrete
items.body: The governance-critique down-trigger now names the threshold directly: two or more listed governance sources must publish a material disclosure or screening gap finding.

items.headline: Promise Delivery stays visibly tracker-only
items.body: The expanded tracker card now shows its own trigger traceability without using grade language, and stale copy about future GPA removal was replaced with current tracker-only wording.

summary: Traceability cleanup follow-on: the audit now matches the live model, Defence & Trade carries an explicit split tripwire, and several easy trigger links were filled in.

items.headline: Consistency audit corrected to match the live tracker / scoring split
items.body: The new consistency self-audit no longer describes Promise Delivery as a live graded file. It now treats Promise Delivery as what the product already is: a derivative accountability tracker that sits outside the 11 performance grades.

items.headline: Defence & Trade now carries a visible split-promotion rule
items.body: The file still stays combined for now, but the methodology now says what breaks that structure: if the defence and trade sub-scores move in opposite directions for two consecutive review cycles, the split shadow promotes into live separate files.

items.headline: Another batch of trigger links was threaded
items.body: Climate, immigration, and housing now carry a few more direct trigger-source links where the public source home already existed, reducing the number of move conditions that still rely on label-only references.

items.headline: Promise Delivery no longer carries a live-grade field in current data
items.body: The tracker still keeps its internal accountability logic, but the live dimension data no longer exposes Promise Delivery as if it were a peer A–F score inside the current board.

summary: Traceability pass: grade-change triggers now carry their own source labels, exception files are framed more honestly, and source stacks are rebalanced into a tighter band.

items.headline: One-notch grade triggers now point at their own source homes
items.body: Move-up and move-down conditions are no longer just free-floating editorial text. Each trigger now carries its own source label, and where a public document exists, a direct source link appears immediately underneath it in the scoring drawer.

items.headline: Readers no longer have to infer which source backs which trigger
items.body: Expanded dimension cards now render a small source line under every one-notch trigger. That means the chain from grade to move condition to supporting source is shorter and more explicit than before.

items.headline: Thin and overloaded source stacks were rebalanced
items.body: Affordability Response, Housing Supply, and Promise Delivery now carry stronger public source trails, while Economic Policy Response was thinned back from a kitchen-sink stack to the same tighter 5-8 source band used elsewhere on the dashboard.

items.headline: Exception files are framed more honestly
items.body: Defence & Trade now explains why it remains one mixed file, and Flagship Delivery now identifies itself more clearly as a derived rollup instead of reading like a normal home dimension.

summary: Trust-feedback pass: the scorecard now explains what it is and is not for, makes freshness harder to miss, and shows where judgment enters each grade.

items.headline: Scorecard framing made explicit
items.body: The Scorecard view now opens with a compact plain-language note: this is a public performance scorecard built from thresholds, source links, and review dates; it is not a forecast, voting guide, popularity measure, or claim that only measurable files matter.

items.headline: Freshness is more visible
items.body: The header now treats the global Updated date as a visible badge, and each dimension's Last reviewed date is styled as a stronger review marker instead of a quiet italic footer.

items.headline: Judgment calls surfaced on every graded card
items.body: Each graded dimension now has a short card-face Judgment call line and a longer Where judgment enters explanation in the scoring drawer, so readers can separate source evidence, thresholds, and editor judgment.

items.headline: Mobile trust surfaces tightened
items.body: On narrow screens, the Scorecard framing now renders as a compact visible panel, Last reviewed pills use stronger contrast, and the Promises tab summary wraps cleanly so statuses like Abandoned are not clipped.

summary: Mobile scoreboard drill-downs now scroll into view, methodology shorthand was removed from the card surface, and the visitor counter is visible again with a same-origin fallback that no longer overlaps the mobile header.

items.headline: Visitor counter restored with a mobile-safe placement
items.body: The sitewide visitor count is back with a same-origin fallback, so browsers that block third-party analytics requests still show a real number instead of a missing badge. On phones, the badge now drops into normal flow above the title instead of floating over it.

items.headline: Headline-score panels now come into view on mobile
items.body: Tapping Household Impact, Full Policy Audit, or Approval Signal on a phone no longer leaves the opened detail panel far below the scoreboard strip. The dashboard now scrolls the panel into view automatically.

items.headline: Internal shorthand pills removed from dimension cards
items.body: Surface labels like "Credit-claiming penalty," "Sub-score file," and "Long-lag file" were removed from the card face. The underlying scoring logic still exists, but it now lives in the expanded explanation instead of reading like internal shorthand on the surface.

items.headline: Scoring adjustments rewritten in plainer language
items.body: Expanded card explanations now use reader-facing labels such as "External pressure," "Early-cycle adjustment," and "Credit reduced for overclaiming" instead of internal modifier names.

summary: Inspectability pass: headline scores now show their math, Major Projects is graded on cohort progress, and the scoring drawer carries a confidence / attribution / lag glossary.

items.headline: Headline scores now show how they're built
items.body: Both the Household Impact and Full Policy Audit cards have a new "How is this score built?" toggle. Click it and the dashboard shows the per-dimension grade, the points, the weight, and the arithmetic that produces the headline letter — so any reader can verify the score against the cards.

items.headline: Major Projects regraded on cohort progress, not first-event triggers
items.body: The Major Projects rubric now defines the project universe (16 projects across 3 MPO tranches as of April 2026) and grades on documented post-designation movement, not just promoted stage labels. The dimension card carries the full project list with each project's current stage and source link. As of 2026-04-30, 4 projects sit above designated status, but only 2 of 16 (~13%) show later-dated post-designation advancement in the recorded cohort data — which keeps the file at C.

items.headline: Confidence / Attribution / Lag glossary inside the scoring drawer
items.body: The three small pills at the top of every dimension's scoring drawer now sit above a one-click "What do these mean?" definition box: a one-sentence explanation each for confidence, attribution, and lag, with the level cutoffs spelled out (High / Medium / Low; Direct / Mixed / Mostly inherited; Short / Medium / Long / Event-driven).

summary: Methodology hardening pass: all dimensions now surface scoring logic, threshold language tightened, and Economic Policy / Ethics source gaps narrowed.

items.headline: Scoring drawers expanded across the dashboard
items.body: Every dimension now exposes its construct, threshold ladder, move triggers, and guardrails inside the card, instead of limiting that transparency to only three audited files.

items.headline: Threshold language tightened across the rubric
items.body: The rubric and canonical scoring sheets were rewritten to use more explicit counts, ranges, and decision rules, with less reliance on words like “credible,” “substantive,” or “material” standing alone.

items.headline: Economic Policy now tracks non-spending levers explicitly
items.body: The live file now surfaces business investment, tax competitiveness, internal-trade execution, regulatory-burden work, and permitting-adjacent checks alongside AI and critical-minerals funding.

items.headline: Ethics challenge stack broadened
items.body: Ethics & Transparency now includes the House ETHI report on the Conflict of Interest Act alongside Democracy Watch and official commissioner materials, reducing dependence on a single advocacy voice.

summary: Majority government confirmed, climate grade moved down to D, new public-approval signal at the top, and a readability pass across the dashboard.

items.headline: Climate & Environment moved D+ → D
items.body: Canada is tracking for about half of its required 2030 emissions reduction. Industrial carbon credits are trading near $20/t despite a $95 headline. ECCC is losing 840+ positions. The PM has acknowledged targets will be missed.
drivers: Industrial credits detached from headline price

items.headline: Majority government confirmed
items.body: Carney's Liberals won 3 Toronto/Quebec byelections on April 13, 2026, reaching 174 seats and securing a majority in the House of Commons.

items.headline: Federal gas tax suspension announced
items.body: Federal fuel excise suspended April 20 through September 7, 2026. Estimated $2.4B in foregone revenue over the window.

items.headline: Approval Signal added to the top of the dashboard
items.body: 60-day rolling average of approve/disapprove across five included pollsters (Léger, Abacus, Ipsos, Angus Reid Institute, Innovative Research). Tracked beside the grades but explicitly not one of them — popularity is not performance.

items.headline: Readability pass on the dashboard
items.body: Plainer card labels, shorter status lines, a new "Limits of this model" note in the Rubric tab, a per-dimension "Last reviewed" line, and an across-the-board font-size bump for mobile.

summary: Climate grade revision (since rolled forward), source stack broadened, probation dimensions normalized to whole-letter C.

items.headline: Source stack expanded
items.body: Added Canadian Climate Institute, IFSD, IRPP / Policy Options, La Presse, Toronto Star, National Observer, and The Conversation Canada to the graded dimensions.

items.headline: Probation dimensions normalized to whole-letter C
items.body: Ethics & Transparency and Flagship Delivery now score as whole letters only (no plus/minus precision behind the displayed grade).
